facts.fact: Lands Minister of State Harriet Ntabazi said the ministry's survey, mapping and registration departments have been equipped with upgraded digital systems, a blockchain-based land records system has been developed, and satellite and drones will be used to capture parcels.
Minister Ntabazi said that with the new digitalisation system applicants enter their data in the computer at district level and have their title printed.

facts.fact: The Minister of Lands, Housing and Urban Development, Judith Nabakooba, described the Uganda National Land Information System (UGNLIS) as a public portal where citizens can check land status, confirm ownership and track transactions.

The Minister said citizens can check land status and confirm ownership on the UGNLIS public portal, and the author urged landowners to check land interests through digitalised land services before transactions.

facts.fact: Lands Permanent Secretary Okalany said more than 1.5 million land titles have already been digitised under the new system.
Okalany said landowners can verify their land status online or through the ministry's mobile application for 10,000 Ugandan shillings.

facts.fact: The Monitor reports that Uganda's digital land registration system, UgNLIS, is in service at the Jinja zonal office, with old records still being digitised.

Uganda's Ministry of Finance reforms tracker, confirmed 11 August 2026, says the National Land Information System (UgNLIS) is operational in 22 zonal offices, with expansion to all land offices in progress.
